items.title: Is IBM Stock A Buy After Missing On Transaction Processing?
items.summary: International Business Machines (IBM) has given back 12.9% over the past three months and sits at $239.94, about 73% of its 52-week high. Management sees no evidence of clients moving off the mainframe. What has changed is that a key slice of IBM’s transactional software revenue rides on a purchase those clients have learned they can postpone.

items.title: Bank FOMO fueling AI spending, Accenture exec says
items.summary: Most banks have yet to see widespread, sustained value from AI initiatives, because they “have not figured out how to reconfigure the work, fully, around AI yet,” said Accenture’s Mike Abbott.

items.title: Is Accenture's Business Falling As Fast As Its Stock?
items.summary: Accenture (ACN) trades at $179.03, about 53% below its two-year high, the price of a business the market thinks is ending. Over the last twelve months, it generated $12.58 billion of free cash flow, a yield of 11.5% on its market value against a 4.4% median for the S&P 500. Both facts are true. The argument between them is about growth.

items.title: 2 Reasons to Watch ACN and 1 to Stay Cautious
items.summary: Over the past six months, Accenture’s stock price fell to $178.52. Shareholders have lost 14.7% of their capital, which is disappointing considering the S&P 500 has climbed by 13.6%. This was partly driven by its softer quarterly results and might have investors contemplating their next move.
